sections.title: Colored Jones polynomial of figure eight knot and non-perturbative topological recursion
sections.abstract: The authors prove that the all-order asymptotic expansion of the figure-eight knot's colored Jones polynomial is related to non-perturbative topological recursion on its elliptic spectral curve.
sections.claimed_result: In the introduction's Theorem 1.1, the authors identify logarithmic differentials of the colored-Jones asymptotic wave function, the recursion wave function, and the matched non-perturbative recursion wave function to all stable orders.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: For the figure-eight knot and its specified elliptic spectral curve; the comparison matches the initial disk and amplitude terms of the wave functions.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem compares formal/asymptotic objects with different domains of definition, whose analytic behavior requires careful treatment; the result is not stated for general knots.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 1.00, entirely from four cross-lists; spans algebraic geometry and geometric topology as well as mathematical physics. Its knot-invariant/topological-recursion bridge places it first among tied highest-score candidates.

sections.title: Noise-induced Extinction in Hierarchical Food Webs
sections.abstract: For hierarchical food webs with omnivory, the authors develop a large-deviation account of demographic-noise-driven extinction networks and derive recursive mean-extinction-time formulas.
sections.claimed_result: Under the stated model, the authors classify feasible communities and their stability, obtain closed-form fluctuational fixed points, and derive an exact recursion for mean extinction times over a network with 3^(N-1) transitions; for three species they compute route actions numerically and compare predictions with stochastic simulations.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The hierarchical model has a basal reproducing species, consumers may prey on every lower species, trophic conversion efficiency is one, and self-limitation acts only on the basal species.
sections.unique_caveat: The general classification depends on these interaction and efficiency assumptions; the three-species instanton actions are numerical rather than closed-form results.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 1.00 from four cross-lists, including dynamical systems and probability. The general-N extinction-network result and the worked three-species case give it the second position in the top score tier.

sections.title: Equivariant K-homology of affine Grassmannians of orthogonal groups
sections.abstract: The authors construct symmetric-function models for torus-equivariant K-homology of affine Grassmannians in types B and D, representing both Schubert structure-sheaf and boundary ideal-sheaf classes.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 5.2 identifies the torus-equivariant K-homology algebra for types B and D with an algebra of constructed symmetric functions, matching Schubert structure sheaves and boundary ideal sheaves with explicit basis elements.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Affine Grassmannians of orthogonal types B and D and their torus-equivariant K-homology, with equivariant parameters retained.
sections.unique_caveat: Equivariant parameters are essential in type D: specializing them to zero can identify distinct Schubert classes, so the result does not simply give an equally faithful nonequivariant model.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.75 from three cross-lists across algebraic geometry, combinatorics, K-theory, and representation theory; the explicit type-B/D realization and stated algebra isomorphism rank it highest in this score tier.

sections.title: Time-consistency of cash-subadditive risk measures: The infimal cocycle property
sections.abstract: The authors characterize time consistency of convex cash-subadditive dynamic risk measures using an attained infimal cocycle condition on their minimal penalties.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show that time consistency is equivalent to an infimal cocycle property of the minimal penalty, with the infimum attained; in the cash-additive case this reduces to the classical cocycle property.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: On L-infinity, continuity from below is assumed; on L^p for finite p, the abstract states no continuity assumption. The dual variables are conditional sub-probability densities.
sections.unique_caveat: The equivalence is stated for the specified convex, cash-subadditive framework and depends on the function-space hypotheses; it should not be read as a characterization of arbitrary dynamic risk measures.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.75 from three cross-lists, including probability and optimization/control; the paper gives an equivalence theorem and connects it to dynamic programming for BSDE-induced risks.

sections.title: Fast Algorithms for Permanents of Permutationally-Dominant Matrices
sections.abstract: The authors give a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for permanents of permutationally-dominant matrices, using a polymer representation and importance sampling.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract claims an FPRAS with runtime quadratic in both matrix dimension and inverse approximation error, based on a polymer-model representation and sampling the logarithm of its partition function.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The guarantee applies to the paper's class of permutationally-dominant matrices, not to arbitrary matrices.
sections.unique_caveat: The approximation result is restricted to that matrix class; the abstract does not claim a general-purpose permanent algorithm with this runtime.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.75 from three cross-lists, including combinatorics; the explicit approximation guarantee and runtime make it a strong algorithmic result within this tier.

sections.title: Reflection subgroups and the Lookup Conjecture
sections.abstract: The authors prove the Lookup Conjecture and its affine type-A extension, relating Bruhat-graph criteria to rational smoothness of Schubert varieties, and establish a parabolic version for the type-A affine Grassmannian.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove the original Boe-Graham conjecture, its A-tilde-n extension, and a parabolic version for the type-A affine Grassmannian, with a stronger Bruhat-graph degree monotonicity property in the latter setting.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The original criterion concerns Schubert varieties in a complex reductive group's flag variety; the extension concerns affine Kac-Moody type A-tilde-n and the type-A affine Grassmannian.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say extension to other Kac-Moody groups would require checking the rank-three reflection subgroups of the corresponding Weyl group.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.50 from two cross-lists in algebraic geometry and representation theory; a named conjecture resolution and a parabolic extension give it priority within this score tier.

sections.title: Sharp decay and regularity thresholds for Minkowski stability in spherical symmetry
sections.abstract: For the spherically symmetric Einstein-scalar field system, the authors prove borderline small-data stability thresholds and construct trapped spheres below either threshold.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove global closeness to Minkowski spacetime and future causal geodesic completeness for small smooth characteristic data at borderline decay and half-derivative regularity, and show both thresholds are sharp by constructing initially untrapped data that form trapped spheres below them.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The theorem is for spherical symmetry and small smooth characteristic data measured in weighted derivative seminorms in the Einstein-scalar field system.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is confined to spherical symmetry; it does not settle corresponding threshold questions without that symmetry restriction.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.50 from two cross-lists, including analysis of PDEs; the paired stability and sharpness claims provide a concrete mathematical result within this score tier.

sections.title: Prophet Inequalities for Mixtures of I.I.D. Random Variables
sections.abstract: In a sequential selection problem with an unknown latent component governing conditionally i.i.d. nonnegative observations, the authors determine the best worst-case prophet-inequality factor as 1/e + 1/k^(2/3+o(1)).
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that the largest universally guaranteed fraction of the expected maximum is 1/e + 1/k^(2/3+o(1)); they give a secretary-rule lower bound and a common-scale-model upper-bound construction.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A latent index J is drawn from a known prior over k component distributions; conditional on J, observations are i.i.d. from a known nonnegative distribution, while J is not observed. The expected maximum is finite.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated correction is asymptotic in the number k of mixture components, and the model assumes the prior and all component distributions are known to the selector.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.50 from two cross-lists spanning statistics, algorithms, and optimization; the matching upper/lower guarantee with an explicit asymptotic factor is the differentiator within this tier.

sections.title: Schwinger-Dyson recursion, Gröbner elimination and graph combinatorics
sections.abstract: The authors use Gröbner elimination to close zero-dimensional Schwinger-Dyson systems and derive linear-arithmetic-operation recursions for counting labelled 9- and 10-regular graphs.
sections.claimed_result: For labelled 9- and 10-regular graphs on n vertices, the authors derive a finite-depth, finite-width recursion that computes total graph counts in O(n) arithmetic operations.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The method uses zero-dimensional QFT with polynomial actions, interpreted as multivariate Gaussian integrals with polynomial insertions, and applies the stated counting result to degrees 9 and 10.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract's linear-operation result is specific to 9- and 10-regular graph counts; it does not state the same complexity for arbitrary degrees or graph-counting problems.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.50 from two cross-lists, including combinatorics; the paper bridges algebraic elimination, mathematical physics, and graph enumeration with a concrete complexity claim.

sections.title: Generic non-convergence of low-temperature Ising Glauber dynamics on Z^2
sections.abstract: At sufficiently low positive temperature, a dense G-delta set of translation-invariant initial laws for the two-dimensional zero-field Ising heat-bath dynamics has both plus and minus phases as subsequential limits, so distributional convergence is meagre.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove the dense-G-delta and meagreness statements for nearest-neighbour, zero-field Ising dynamics on Z^2; they state the conclusion also applies to all reversible monotone Glauber dynamics for the Ising model.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Initial laws are translation invariant, the temperature is sufficiently low and positive, and genericity is in the weak topology on the space of such laws.
sections.unique_caveat: Generic here is topological, not a probability-one claim; the theorem is limited to a low-temperature regime and the specified dynamics and initial-law space.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.25 from one cross-list into mathematical physics; the paper also gives a partial answer to a stated open problem about convergence of Ising dynamics.

sections.title: Irreducible trinomials over the binary field: an elliptic-curve criterion and explicit families
sections.abstract: The authors give an elliptic-curve and reciprocity criterion for a family of binary trinomials and construct infinite irreducible-trinomial families in fourteen reduced exponent classes.
sections.claimed_result: For k >= 2, the authors prove that X^((4^k+2)/3)+X+1 is irreducible over F_2 exactly when 4^k+3 is prime and 2 is a primitive root modulo that prime, and they give explicit infinite families in fourteen reduced exponent classes.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The criterion concerns the displayed trinomial over the binary field and integers k >= 2; the family construction uses power substitution and linearization.
sections.unique_caveat: The criterion is for a specific exponent family; the abstract does not claim a complete classification of all irreducible binary trinomials.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.25 from one cross-list between number theory and algebraic geometry; the paper's explicit if-and-only-if criterion makes it a notable cross-field result among remaining score-tier candidates.
